description: Faults a reader must detect no later than decoding the faulty data. Each request is an unbounded range whose limit covers every row (projecting the faulty column where the fault is in values), so it decodes the faulty page under any correct access path. Core examples: hand-reviewed; their expectations are authoritative.

cases.description: Rows 2 and 3 (one page) are stored in descending order. open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with key_order (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).

Row group 0 ends with k06 and row group 1 starts with k05. open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with key_order (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).

Part 0 ends with k09, part 1 starts with k05. The manifest hides this by declaring part 0's max key as k04 (so the manifest bounds look disjoint). open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with key_order or bounds_mismatch (an earlier refusal with that code also passes). The fault is hidden by declaring part 0's max key below its actual last key, so the manifest bounds also differ from the decoded keys.

The first key of the only part is empty (it still sorts first). open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with invalid_key or bounds_mismatch (an earlier refusal with that code also passes). A manifest cannot express an empty min key (base64 minLength 4), so it names the second key; a reader that compares first keys on open may report bounds_mismatch.

non-utf8-keys with the key annotated STRING: two keys (each mid-page) are not valid UTF-8; every page bound is. open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with invalid_key (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).

Row group 1 holds a 5002-byte key; pyarrow omits the whole ColumnIndex of that key chunk (statistics larger than its 4096-byte limit) but keeps the OffsetIndex. open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with missing_page_index (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).

Column h is FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY(4) in part 0 and FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY(8) in part 1. open may succeed; an unbounded range, which routes to both parts, must be refused with inconsistent_column (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).

Row group 0's key OffsetIndex says first_row_index [0, 1, 4] for pages of 2 rows each: page 0 holds 2 rows but its indexed interval is 1 row. open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with invalid_page_index (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).

Row group 0's key OffsetIndex locates page 1 one byte after its real header. open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with invalid_page_index (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).

The key ColumnIndex max of the page ending at 0xFF*80 0x02 is shortened to 0xFF*16, which is below the page's keys (the all-0xFF truncation fault RG-5 forbids). open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with invalid_page_index (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).

The STRING key's ColumnIndex max for the page ending at row-01 is row-\xff: still an upper bound, but not valid UTF-8 (KEY-6). open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with invalid_page_index (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).

The dictionary page of column s in part 0, row group 0 is malformed: its first value claims a length of 2^31-1 bytes. open may succeed; an unbounded range that decodes the faulty data must be refused with invalid_parquet (an earlier refusal with that code also passes).
